findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 1 exercise as printed on PDF 19-21 (printed pages 19-21; the MCQs begin on p19 under the chapter's EXERCISE heading), in the book's words and order.

Counts: Q.1 twelve MCQs (I-XII, options a-d), Q.2 thirteen short-answer questions (a-m; m with parts (i), (ii) kept in one self-check), Descriptive Questions Q.3-Q.6 (four); all solved in English and Roman Urdu.

The book prints no answer key. MCQ keys worked out from the chapter: I a, II c, III b, IV c, V a, VI a, VII d, VIII a, IX c, X b, XI b, XII d. MCQ I is keyed (a) Newlands because the chapter (1.1) says Newlands 'first time observed periodicity' (Döbereiner's triads, 1829, came earlier but the chapter does not call them periodicity).

Book corrections (kept as printed, Book correction box after the item): MCQ VII option (d) and Short Q (h) print 'Phosphorous' / 'phosphorous' for the element phosphorus; Short Q (e) prints 'for the the increasing reactivity'. Descriptive Q.3: the chapter's own equations 2Na + O2 -> 2Na2O2 (unbalanced), 2MgO(g) and Mg + 2H2O(g) -> MgO + H2 (unbalanced; not marked in the chapter's lesson) are corrected in the answer with a Book correction box; Q.4 uses the balanced P2O3 + 3H2O -> 2H3PO3 (Wazahat box in Roman Urdu).
Short Q (k) is printed as a statement without a question; answered as 'explain why'. Short Q (m): MgCl2 classed neutral as in the chapter (1.9.2, pH 6.5).

Answers beyond the chapter, labelled here: Short Q (m) uses the hydrolysis PCl5 + 4H2O -> H3PO4 + 5HCl (the chapter gives only PCl3 and asks students to predict PCl5 in Quick Check 1.8); Short Q (j) quotes IE values of He 2372 and Li 520 kJ/mol (standard values); Q.5 explains the low F electron affinity by electron repulsion in its small 2p shell (the chapter only states the order).
Comparison answer Q.3 (Na vs Mg) carries a two-column answer table. No diagram questions in this exercise. Draft for the academic review.
